ballarat-1.name: Sovereign Hill
ballarat-1.bio: Open-air museum of 1850s Ballarat where you can pan for real gold and take an underground mine tour.

ballarat-2.name: Eureka Centre
ballarat-2.bio: Interpretive centre in Eureka Stockade Memorial Park with an exhibition on the Eureka Rebellion and the Eureka Flag.

ballarat-4.name: Art Gallery of Ballarat
ballarat-4.bio: Australia's oldest regional art gallery, founded 1884 and free, currently showing at Backspace Gallery, Mair Street.

ballarat-5.name: Lake Wendouree
ballarat-5.bio: Shallow artificial urban lake beside the suburb of Wendouree, with heritage trams running along its shore.

ballarat-6.name: Ballarat Botanical Gardens
ballarat-6.bio: 40-hectare gardens on Lake Wendouree's western shore, a Victorian-style garden flanked by North and South Gardens.

ballarat-7.name: Ballarat Wildlife Park
ballarat-7.bio: Zoo with over 300 animals, including over 100 free-roaming kangaroos, and hand-feeding of kangaroos and koalas.

ballarat-8.name: Kryal Castle
ballarat-8.bio: Replica medieval castle at Leigh Creek, 8 km east of Ballarat, open to visitors since 1974 with overnight stays.

ballarat-10.name: Ballarat Tramway Museum
ballarat-10.bio: Volunteer-run museum where heritage trams run around Lake Wendouree and the Botanical Gardens on weekends.

ballarat-11.name: Clunes
ballarat-11.bio: Gold-rush town north of Ballarat, site of Victoria's first registered gold find and home to second-hand bookshops.

ballarat-12.name: Blue Waters Lake
ballarat-12.bio: Former open-cut mine filled with water in Creswick Regional Park, an 800 m walk from the first car park.

ballarat-13.name: Ballarat to Skipton Rail Trail
ballarat-13.bio: A 53 km rail trail along the old Skipton railway line from Ballarat through Haddon, Smythesdale and Pittong.

bendigo-1.name: Bendigo Art Gallery
bendigo-1.bio: One of Australia's oldest regional art galleries, with 19th-century European and Australian art and free entry.

bendigo-2.name: Central Deborah Gold Mine
bendigo-2.bio: Disused gold mine with a 75-minute tour 61 m underground, plus surface heritage buildings and a museum.

bendigo-3.name: Golden Dragon Museum
bendigo-3.bio: Museum of Chinese Australian history in Bendigo's Dai Gum San precinct, with Chinese gardens and a Kuan Yin temple.

bendigo-4.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Bendigo
bendigo-4.bio: Gothic Revival cathedral with an 87 m spire, one of Australia's largest churches, completed in 1977.

bendigo-5.name: Rosalind Park
bendigo-5.bio: 60-acre park beside Bendigo's centre with a conservatory, fernery and the Poppet Head Lookout Tower.

bendigo-7.name: Greater Bendigo National Park
bendigo-7.bio: 17,020-hectare park of Box-Ironbark forest near Bendigo, with spring wildflowers and the Old Tom Mine Walk.

daylesford-1.name: Lake Daylesford
daylesford-1.bio: Lake in Daylesford dammed in 1929 to a Walter Burley Griffin design, and used for fishing.

daylesford-2.name: Wombat Hill Botanic Gardens
daylesford-2.bio: Heritage-listed 19th-century botanic gardens on Wombat Hill, with a fern gully and conifers for a walk or picnic.

daylesford-3.name: Hepburn Mineral Springs Reserve
daylesford-3.bio: Reserve of mineral springs at Hepburn Springs, used for drinking and bathing since the 1860s, with free pumps.

daylesford-4.name: Convent Gallery
daylesford-4.bio: Former convent on Wombat Hill with seven gallery spaces, museums, a chapel and gardens over four levels.

daylesford-5.name: Hepburn Regional Park
daylesford-5.bio: Regional park around Daylesford with waterfalls, mineral springs, gold-rush relics and Jacksons Lookout tower.

daylesford-6.name: Mineral Springs Loop Walk
daylesford-6.bio: Loop walk in Hepburn Regional Park past mineral springs, with a view of Sailors Falls.

daylesford-7.name: Hepburn Springs
daylesford-7.bio: Spa town in Australia's largest concentration of mineral springs, with free spring pumps and a bathhouse.

daylesford-8.name: Trentham Falls
daylesford-8.bio: Waterfall dropping over 32 m down basalt, the highest single drop in Central Victoria, near Trentham.

macedon-ranges-1.name: Hanging Rock
macedon-ranges-1.bio: Former volcano rising 105 m above the plain, with a sealed summit trail and the setting of Picnic at Hanging Rock.

macedon-ranges-3.name: Mount Macedon Memorial Cross
macedon-ranges-3.bio: 21 m First World War memorial cross of terracotta tiles near the summit of Mount Macedon, visible from the plains.

macedon-ranges-4.name: Kyneton
macedon-ranges-4.bio: Town in the Macedon Ranges with Piper Street's original buildings, botanic gardens and Campaspe River walks.

macedon-ranges-5.name: Woodend
macedon-ranges-5.bio: Town between Melbourne and Bendigo, a gold-rush thoroughfare near Mount Macedon, Hanging Rock and waterfalls.

macedon-ranges-6.name: Kyneton Botanic Gardens
macedon-ranges-6.bio: Botanic gardens established in 1858, with bluestone walls, a rotunda and a riverside walk on the Campaspe.

macedon-ranges-7.name: Turpin Falls
macedon-ranges-7.bio: An 18 m basalt waterfall on the Campaspe River north of Kyneton, reached by a short path and staircase.

castlemaine-1.name: Maldon
castlemaine-1.bio: Gold-rush town 19 km from Castlemaine, named Australia's first notable town in 1966, with a mine open to the public.

castlemaine-2.name: Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park
castlemaine-2.bio: Gold-rush mine relics and puddling machines in Box-Ironbark woodland, with heritage walks near Castlemaine.

castlemaine-3.name: Castlemaine Theatre Royal
castlemaine-3.bio: The Australian mainland's longest continuously operating theatre, now a 200-seat cinema with live music and a bar.

heathcote-graytown-national-park.name: Heathcote-Graytown National Park
heathcote-graytown-national-park.bio: National park of 12,833 hectares by Heathcote, with Mount Ida and Viewing Rock lookouts and picnic areas.

lake-eppalock.name: Lake Eppalock
lake-eppalock.bio: Campaspe River reservoir near Heathcote, ringed by Box Ironbark forest, with boat ramps and fishing.

pink-cliffs-geological-reserve.name: Pink Cliffs Geological Reserve
pink-cliffs-geological-reserve.bio: Former Heathcote gold-mining site where sluicing left a lunar-like landscape of pink and pastel clay cliffs.

o-keefe-rail-trail.name: O'Keefe Rail Trail
o-keefe-rail-trail.bio: A 49 km gravel and sealed rail trail for walking and cycling along a former railway from Bendigo to Heathcote.

maryborough.name: Maryborough
maryborough.bio: Goldfields town north of Ballarat, known for its 1890 railway station with a bell tower that Mark Twain praised.

kooyoora-state-park.name: Kooyoora State Park
kooyoora-state-park.bio: Box-ironbark forest and granite outcrops west of Inglewood, with a 5.3 km Long Rock walk to a lookout.

melville-caves.name: Melville Caves
melville-caves.bio: Granite outcrops and shelters in Kooyoora State Park, a believed bushranger hideout, with a picnic area.

eucalyptus-distillery-museum.name: Eucalyptus Distillery Museum
eucalyptus-distillery-museum.bio: Volunteer-run museum at Inglewood where guided tours show a model distillery extracting oil from eucalyptus leaves.

goldfields-track.name: Goldfields Track
goldfields-track.bio: A 210 km walking and riding track from Ballarat to Bendigo through goldfields towns and forests, doable in sections.

held.reason: Eureka Stockade is the same park as the Eureka Centre (ballarat-2): near-duplicate
